limitations: Derived from PriceCatcher (KPDN and DOSM, data.gov.my) under CC BY 4.0; the compilation is CC0. Not an official Malaysian government product.
State-scoped to Johor. Other states are not represented in this release.

Pairs with fewer than three observations in a week are excluded at the prediction instant; a following week that is too sparse is counted as an unobserved outcome (143,978) rather than dropped silently.
Missing lags are sentinel-coded -1.0, which is unambiguous only because prices are strictly positive.
The holdout is labelled and ships with the release; keep its labels outside an evaluated agent's workspace.
The source feed revises monthly; a later rebuild will not reproduce these bytes.

paragraphs: Malaysia's PriceCatcher programme publishes daily retail prices for hundreds of items across thousands of premises. Access is not the contribution. The contribution is the weekly panel - 397,982 train / 280,468 eval / 154,279 holdout item-premise-weeks in the state of Johor, from November 2023 to October 2026 - and the declaration that the prediction instant is the end of week W: a forecast made on Sunday night about next week's shelf price.

The label is a direction call, not a level: will the weekly modal price be higher in week W+1 than in week W. Positive rates run 14.9% / 17.5% / 20.4%, and the rise of the rate across the windows is itself a signal about the period.

The baseline is strong enough to be interesting: the harness's XGBoost pass reaches 0.7520 eval AUC, twenty-one points above the best naive reference (an item-level prior at 0.5354, with momentum and mean-reversion near 0.50). Unlike tasks where persistence wins, this one rewards learning something about the item and the week.
